sentences.en: Hello, welcome to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听《历史的余韵》（The Rest is History）。

sentences.en: The story goes that in the year 860, the Chuds, the Slavs, the Krivichians and the Vess,
sentences.zh: 故事是这样的：公元860年，楚德人、斯拉夫人、克里维奇人和维斯人，

sentences.en: people who live in what we now know as Russia, had fallen out among themselves, needed somebody to rule them.
sentences.zh: 也就是生活在今天我们所知的俄罗斯这片土地上的人们，他们之间发生了内讧，需要有人来统治他们。

sentences.en: So they turned to the Vikings.
sentences.zh: 于是他们求助于维京人。

sentences.en: Our land is great and rich, they supposedly said, but there is no order in it.
sentences.zh: 他们大概是这样说的：我们的土地辽阔而富饶，但这里毫无秩序。

sentences.en: Come to rule and reign over us.
sentences.zh: 请来统治我们，做我们的君主吧。

sentences.en: And the person who accepted that offer was a man called Rurik, one of three brothers, Rurik, Sinius and Truvor.
sentences.zh: 接受这个提议的人是一个叫留里克（Rurik）的人，他是三兄弟之一，另外两位是西涅乌斯（Sinius）和特鲁沃尔（Truvor）。

sentences.en: Very close to Trevor, weirdly.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，这名字和特雷弗（Trevor）很像。

sentences.en: Rurik.
sentences.zh: 留里克。

sentences.en: You couldn't take a Viking chieftain.
sentences.zh: 你没法带走一个维京首领。

sentences.en: Seriously, Trevor.
sentences.zh: 说真的，特雷弗。

sentences.en: Rurik established himself in a place which we now know as Novgorod and his successors later moved to Kiev.
sentences.zh: 留里克在今天我们所知的诺夫哥罗德定居下来，他的继任者后来迁往了基辅。

sentences.en: And it's from that story that the countries of Russia, Belarus and Ukraine all trace their history.
sentences.zh: 正是从这个故事开始，俄罗斯、白俄罗斯和乌克兰这几个国家追溯着它们的历史。

sentences.en: Tom, we did the origins of the Vikings in the East yesterday.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们昨天讲了维京人在东方的起源。

sentences.en: Do you think there's any truth to this story at all?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这个故事有任何真实性吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think the obvious parallel with this, if you are in Britain, is with the Dukes of Normandy, which likewise has a kind of almost mythic origin story.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得如果你身处英国，这与诺曼底公爵的故事有着明显的相似之处，那同样有着一种近乎神话般的起源故事。

sentences.en: So it's Rollo who is given this land by the Frankish king.
sentences.zh: 罗洛（Rollo）就是从法兰克国王那里得到了这片土地。

sentences.en: And all kinds of myths surround this figure.
sentences.zh: 围绕着这个人物有着各种各样的神话。

sentences.en: I mean, he probably existed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他很可能确实存在过。

sentences.en: He probably wasn't called Rollo, though, was he?
sentences.zh: 不过他可能不叫罗洛，对吧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Tom Shippey in his book about the Vikings calls him Ganga Rolf, which I think is a much better name.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·希皮（Tom Shippey）在他关于维京人的书中称他为“步行者罗尔夫”（Ganga Rolf），我觉得这名字好听多了。

sentences.en: So there are all kinds of stories about how he founds Normandy and about how the original Normans are not just Vikings, but they're people from all kinds of different backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 所以关于他如何建立诺曼底，以及最初的诺曼人不仅仅是维京人，而是来自各种不同背景的人，有着各种各样的故事。

sentences.en: And he establishes this duchy.
sentences.zh: 他建立了这个公国。

sentences.en: And the question of whether William the Conqueror, the most famous of the Dukes of Normandy, is he a Viking?
sentences.zh: 那么问题来了，诺曼底公爵中最著名的威廉征服者（William the Conqueror），他是维京人吗？

sentences.en: Is he French?
sentences.zh: 他是法国人吗？

sentences.en: What is he exactly?
sentences.zh: 他到底是什么人？

sentences.en: I think that that sheds a kind of really interesting light on the process of state formation in Novgorod, but even more particularly in Kiev.
sentences.zh: 我认为这为诺夫哥罗德，尤其是基辅的国家形成过程提供了一个非常有趣的视角。

sentences.en: And obviously the background to this, as in the West, so in the East, it's about the way that the Vikings are moving into strange lands,
sentences.zh: 显然，这背后的背景，无论是在西方还是东方，都是关于维京人如何进入陌生的土地，

sentences.en: establishing Viking polities that nevertheless take on the lineaments of the lands and the cultures and the peoples that they're settling among.
sentences.zh: 建立起维京政体，但同时又吸收了他们所定居土地的文化、习俗和人民的特征。

sentences.en: Well, that's a very controversial subject there, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是一个非常有争议的话题，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because how much that's the case has been bitterly contested by academics.
sentences.zh: 因为这种情况到底有多少，一直受到学术界的激烈争论。

sentences.en: How Viking are they?
sentences.zh: 他们到底有多“维京”？

sentences.en: For those people who didn't listen to yesterday, I can't believe there was anybody who didn't listen to yesterday's podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 对于那些没听昨天节目的人，我简直不敢相信还有人没听昨天的播客。

sentences.en: But we did the sort of first hundred years.
sentences.zh: 但我们讲了最初的一百年左右。

sentences.en: So the Vikings have been what we, I mean, Vikings is actually the wrong word because they're not really.
sentences.zh: 所以维京人已经……我的意思是，“维京人”这个词其实用错了，因为他们并不完全是。

sentences.en: The Rus.
sentences.zh: 是“罗斯人”（Rus）。

sentences.en: Which is going to start to take on, as Tom said, it's not just the liniments of the culture around it, but the liniments of a state.
sentences.zh: 正如汤姆所说，它开始不仅具备周围文化的特征，还具备了国家的特征。

sentences.en: And how quickly it does that is, again, debatable.
sentences.zh: 至于它形成得有多快，这同样是有争议的。

sentences.en: So the sort of origin story that's told is that the, which is very flattering, by the way, to their Scandinavian self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 所以，流传下来的起源故事——顺便说一句，这对他们的斯堪的纳维亚自尊心非常讨好——

sentences.en: You could say it's a kind of slightly colonial story, is that the surrounding peoples are so shambolic and kind of disorganized and backward.
sentences.zh: 你可以说这是一个稍微带点殖民色彩的故事，即周围的民族是如此混乱、无组织且落后。

sentences.en: They are falling out among themselves and they have to ask the Vikings, the Rus, to come in and rule them.
sentences.zh: 他们陷入内讧，不得不请求维京人，也就是罗斯人，进来统治他们。

sentences.en: And there might be some element of truth in that, don't you think, Tom, that they might, you know,
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你不觉得这其中可能有一点真实成分吗？他们可能，你知道，

sentences.en: appeal to these armed guys in their trading posts to come and help them against a rival clan or a rival tribe.
sentences.zh: 向这些驻扎在贸易站的武装人员求助，让他们帮忙对抗敌对的氏族或部落。

sentences.en: And that's how it starts, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得事情就是这样开始的吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's failing the kind of the brute process by which I think pretty clearly what happens is that you, as we said in the early episode, you know, these, to begin with,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得这忽略了那种粗暴的过程，我认为很明显发生的事情是，正如我们在上一集所说的，你知道，这些，起初，

sentences.en: are trading ventures.
sentences.zh: 是贸易冒险。

sentences.en: And so you have to have transit posts.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须有中转站。

sentences.en: You have to have places where you can not just do deals, not just store things ready for when the rivers become navigable, but also to kind of pick up information.
sentences.zh: 你必须有一些地方，不仅可以进行交易，不仅可以储存货物等待河流通航，还可以收集信息。

sentences.en: You know, you can't survive without that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，没有这些你无法生存。

sentences.en: And we drew the parallel yesterday with trading posts in, say, Canada in the 18th century.
sentences.zh: 我们昨天类比了18世纪加拿大的贸易站。

sentences.en: But it's pretty clear that before long, these transit posts become forts.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，没过多久，这些中转站就变成了堡垒。

sentences.en: Yeah, wooden forts.
sentences.zh: 是的，木制堡垒。

sentences.en: And once they've become forts, then you can do what the Vikings are doing in the West as well, which is basically to kind of set up protection rackets.
sentences.zh: 一旦它们变成了堡垒，你就可以做维京人在西方做的事情，也就是基本上建立起保护费勒索体系。

sentences.en: So what's been a cartel becomes a kind of mafia style operation and you're charging protection money.
sentences.zh: 所以，原本的卡特尔组织变成了一种黑手党式的运作，你开始收取保护费。

sentences.en: And if Rurik existed, and there is a kind of historically tested Rurik at around this time, I think, tested in Scandinavia.
sentences.zh: 如果留里克确实存在——而且我认为在那个时期确实有一位史料记载的留里克，在斯堪的纳维亚有记录。

sentences.en: But whether it's the same person or not is debated.
sentences.zh: 但至于是不是同一个人，还有争议。

sentences.en: But if he existed, I think you could imagine him as the kind of the equivalent of a mafia boss.
sentences.zh: 但如果他存在，我想你可以把他想象成某种黑手党头目。

sentences.en: And then, you know, again, as happens in the West, Normandy being the obvious example, a kind of a protection racket becomes a state.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，同样地，正如在西方发生的那样，诺曼底就是一个明显的例子，一种保护费勒索体系演变成了一个国家。

sentences.en: Well, that's so we know so little about Rurik.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们对留里克知之甚少。

sentences.en: We know that he established himself in Novgorod, which we talked about yesterday.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他在诺夫哥罗德建立了统治，我们昨天谈到过。

sentences.en: And there's a statue of him to this day.
sentences.zh: 直到今天还有他的雕像。

sentences.en: And this is the second half of the 9th century.
sentences.zh: 这是9世纪的下半叶。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is 860, I think it is, is it?
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是860年，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, about 860 to 862 are the dates given.
sentences.zh: 是的，给出的日期大约是860年到862年。

sentences.en: So, by the way, we haven't really talked about sources.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，我们还没怎么谈过史料来源。

sentences.en: This is coming from an incredible source called the Russian Primary Chronicle, which is, as is so often the way, written.
sentences.zh: 这来自一部令人难以置信的史料，叫《俄罗斯初年编年史》（Russian Primary Chronicle），正如通常的情况一样，它是写于……

sentences.en: In the 12th century.
sentences.zh: 12世纪。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: Written at least 200, 300 years later by a monk called Nestor, I think.
sentences.zh: 至少是200、300年后由一位叫内斯特（Nestor）的僧侣写的，我想是这样。

sentences.en: And, you know, is written in very different kind of political and cultural circumstances.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，它是写在非常不同的政治和文化环境下的。

sentences.en: So we, as with so much of early medieval history, we just don't know whether these are legends, whether there is a grain of truth in them,
sentences.zh: 所以，就像中世纪早期的许多历史一样，我们根本不知道这些是传说，还是其中包含了一丝真实，

sentences.en: whether it's retrospective kind of legitimizing.
sentences.zh: 又或者是事后的某种合法化修饰。

sentences.en: I think there must be a grain of truth, because I think that the idea of a kind of dynastic descent from Rurik becomes quite important.
sentences.zh: 我认为一定有一丝真实成分，因为我认为那种源自留里克的王朝血统观念变得非常重要。

sentences.en: So, you know, if Rurik didn't exist, someone of the same name must have.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果留里克不存在，也一定有同名的人存在过。

sentences.en: But, well, someone of the same, but the whole thing, Rurik and two brothers, I mean, all that sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 但是，好吧，同名的人，但整件事，留里克和两个兄弟，我的意思是，所有这些东西。

sentences.en: But there's clearly a dynasty established itself in Novgorod.
sentences.zh: 但显然有一个王朝在诺夫哥罗德建立了起来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That will then expand.
sentences.zh: 然后它会扩张。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's two guys who are, it says in the Russian Primary Chronicle, two men who do not belong to Rurik's kin, but were boyards.
sentences.zh: 所以有两个人，根据《俄罗斯初年编年史》的记载，这两个人不属于留里克的亲属，而是波雅尔（boyards）。

sentences.en: That's the kind of Russian.
sentences.zh: 那是某种俄语词汇。

sentences.en: They're basically captains.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上就是队长。

sentences.en: I don't know what the word is.
sentences.zh: 我不知道确切的词是什么。

sentences.en: They're not nobles.
sentences.zh: 他们不是贵族。

sentences.en: I mean, nobles is the wrong word, but they're sort of, they're members of the gang.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，用贵族这个词不对，但他们是某种，他们是团伙成员。

sentences.en: Would you say that?
sentences.zh: 你会这么说吗？

sentences.en: Soldiers, I guess, is what.
sentences.zh: 我想应该是士兵吧。

sentences.en: Mafia.
sentences.zh: 黑手党。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they basically go off.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上就出发了。

sentences.en: They're called, the Russian Primary Chronicle has them as Askald and Deer.
sentences.zh: 他们被称为，《俄罗斯初年编年史》中称他们为阿斯科尔德（Askald）和迪尔（Deer）。

sentences.en: And as with so many of these names, almost all the names we're talking about, they're slavicized versions of originally Norse names, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 和这么多名字一样，我们谈论的几乎所有名字，它们都是原始诺斯语名字的斯拉夫化版本，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because I think they were Huskuld and Dury, the original, my beautiful, absolutely impeccable Old Norse pronunciation there, Tom.
sentences.zh: 因为我想他们原本是Huskuld和Dury，汤姆，我那美丽、绝对无可挑剔的古诺斯语发音。

sentences.en: I hope you noticed.
sentences.zh: 我希望你注意到了。

sentences.en: They go off down the Dnieper and they come to what the Chronicle says is a city on a hill.
sentences.zh: 他们顺着第聂伯河而下，来到了编年史所说的“山上的城市”。

sentences.en: Again, a little bit too kind of folktale stroke biblical, I think.
sentences.zh: 同样，我觉得这有点太像民间故事或圣经风格了。

sentences.en: Anyway, this place is Kiev and it already exists, being set up by somebody called Ki, hence the name.
sentences.zh: 总之，这个地方就是基辅，它已经存在了，是由一个叫“基”（Ki）的人建立的，名字也由此而来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Askald and Deer supposedly settle in Kiev and say, this is a great place.
sentences.zh: 阿斯科尔德和迪尔据称在基辅定居，并说：这是一个好地方。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously it's a good place because it's further down the river, further towards Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然这是一个好地方，因为它在河流下游，更靠近君士坦丁堡。

sentences.en: So it's kind of makes sense that they've established another fort stroke trading station that becomes their own little polity.
sentences.zh: 所以他们建立了另一个堡垒兼贸易站，并成为他们自己的小政体，这很有道理。

sentences.en: And so the question of whether Kiev is Viking, which, you know, Putin's been worrying about this.
sentences.zh: 所以关于基辅是否是维京人的问题，你知道，普京一直在担心这个问题。

sentences.en: So it's a topical question.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个热门话题。

sentences.en: But again, would you think that maybe, you know, there'd be a parallel perhaps with York?
sentences.zh: 但同样，你认为也许，你知道，这是否可以与约克（York）进行类比？

sentences.en: Yorvik.
sentences.zh: 约维克（Yorvik）。

sentences.en: You know, it's a pre-existing settlement, gets taken over by the Vikings, gets a Viking name.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个预先存在的定居点，被维京人接管，并有了维京名字。

sentences.en: The Vikings rule it and then they gradually get absorbed into the fabric of what, you know, returns to being an English city.
sentences.zh: 维京人统治它，然后他们逐渐被吸收进当地的结构中，最终又变回了一座英国城市。

sentences.en: But perhaps there's, I mean, the parallels are never exact, but there's something there.
sentences.zh: 但也许，我的意思是，类比从来都不完全精确，但确实有相似之处。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Of what's happening in the East as well as the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 东方和西方发生的事情都有相似之处。

sentences.en: Your parallel in Normandy was a really good one.
sentences.zh: 你在诺曼底的类比非常贴切。

sentences.en: I think to people at the time, sort of 9th, 10th century people, our attempts to fix labels on them would seem weird, wouldn't they?
sentences.zh: 我想对于当时的人，也就是9、10世纪的人来说，我们试图给他们贴标签的尝试会显得很奇怪，对吧？

sentences.en: They would say, well, who cares?
sentences.zh: 他们会说，好吧，谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: I mean, what's it to you, what ethnicity?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，什么种族对你来说有什么关系？

sentences.en: The concept wouldn't make an enormous amount of sense to them.
sentences.zh: 这个概念对他们来说不会有太大的意义。

sentences.en: So the question of, you know, are they Slavs, are they Scandinavian, are they Russians, Ukrainians?
sentences.zh: 所以关于，你知道，他们是斯拉夫人，是斯堪的纳维亚人，是俄罗斯人，还是乌克兰人的问题，

sentences.en: I mean, in a sense, it's a very, very anachronistic question.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从某种意义上说，这是一个非常、非常时代错乱的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, what matters to them is who's got the weapons, the power, the money.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对他们来说重要的是谁拥有武器、权力和金钱。

sentences.en: What they are is lads.
sentences.zh: 他们就是一群“小伙子”（lads）。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolute lads.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是小伙子。

sentences.en: They are, but I don't think they're the Bullingdon lads, Tom.
sentences.zh: 他们是，但我不认为他们是布灵顿俱乐部（Bullingdon）的那种小伙子，汤姆。

sentences.en: I think they're much more predatory and brutal because they, so Asgold and Deer, these pair of kind of Viking adventurers, the kin of Rurik, his descent, you know, his heirs,
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们更具掠夺性和残暴性，因为他们，所以阿斯科尔德和迪尔，这一对维京冒险家，留里克的亲属，他的后代，你知道，他的继承人，

sentences.en: if they exist, they're moving in.
sentences.zh: 如果他们存在的话，他们正在进入。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they're like the kind of, you know,
sentences.zh: 他们就像那种，你知道，

sentences.en: the bigger crime family moving in and they take over Kiev and Kiev opens up the access to the Black Sea and beyond the Black Sea lies Miklagard, Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 更大的犯罪家族搬了进来，他们接管了基辅，而基辅打开了通往黑海的通道，在黑海之外就是米克拉加德（Miklagard），即君士坦丁堡。

sentences.en: Yeah, which we haven't talked about at all, which is enjoying, it's a renaissance, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，我们根本没谈过这个，它正在享受，这是一场文艺复兴，不是吗？

sentences.en: Are we not in the Macedonian renaissance at this point, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们现在不是处于马其顿文艺复兴时期吗？

sentences.en: So things, yeah, things are looking up for the Byzantines.
sentences.zh: 所以事情，是的，拜占庭人的情况正在好转。

sentences.en: Yeah, so they still think of themselves as Romans, don't they?
sentences.zh: 是的，所以他们仍然认为自己是罗马人，不是吗？

sentences.en: They do, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实。

sentences.en: They still call themselves the Romanoi.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然称自己为“罗马人”（Romanoi）。

sentences.en: They absolutely think we are Rome, we are the, and they have this massive city.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对认为我们就是罗马，我们是……而且他们拥有这座巨大的城市。

sentences.en: They have tons of money.
sentences.zh: 他们有大量的财富。

sentences.en: They're a very rich and sophisticated culture.
sentences.zh: 他们是一个非常富有和复杂的文明。

sentences.en: And then one day in the year 860, they kind of look out of the window and these, as you said, these lads from their ships have turned up in their ships.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天，在公元860年，他们从窗户往外看，正如你所说，这些来自船上的小伙子们乘着船出现了。

sentences.en: And the patriarch, the Archbishop of Constantinople, a man called Photius, has written this famous description of this.
sentences.zh: 君士坦丁堡的牧首，一位叫佛提乌（Photius）的人，写下了这段著名的描述。

sentences.en: He says, the Russ are an obscure nation, a nation of no account, a nation ranked among slaves, unknown, which has won a name from their expedition against us.
sentences.zh: 他说：罗斯人是一个默默无闻的民族，一个无足轻重的民族，一个被列为奴隶的民族，一个未知的民族，却因对我们的远征而赢得了名声。

sentences.en: So basically, well, the shocking thing for the people of Constantinople is that these utter nobodies, who they regard as so far beneath them, turn up and besiege their city.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，嗯，对君士坦丁堡的人来说，令人震惊的是，这些他们认为远在自己之下的无名小卒，竟然出现并围攻了他们的城市。

sentences.en: And they keep doing this, don't they?
sentences.zh: 而且他们一直在这样做，不是吗？

sentences.en: And they seem to have very good intelligence because they invariably turn up when the imperial fleet is away.
sentences.zh: 而且他们似乎有非常好的情报，因为他们总是出现在帝国舰队不在的时候。

sentences.en: Yeah, or the emperors of campaigning against somebody else.
sentences.zh: 是的，或者皇帝正在远征别人。

sentences.en: So the walls of Constantinople are a great wonder.
sentences.zh: 所以君士坦丁堡的城墙是一个伟大的奇迹。

sentences.en: They are impregnable.
sentences.zh: 它们是坚不可摧的。

sentences.en: But there are obviously all kinds of churches and monasteries, you know, as in England, that are kind of lying exposed.
sentences.zh: 但显然有各种各样的教堂和修道院，你知道，就像在英国一样，它们暴露在外。

sentences.en: And the Vikings have all kind of fun with them, don't they?
sentences.zh: 而维京人在他们身上玩得很开心，不是吗？

sentences.en: They use monks for archery practice.
sentences.zh: 他们用僧侣来练习射箭。

sentences.en: They nail hats on to the heads of priests and all kinds of badinage.
sentences.zh: 他们把帽子钉在牧师的头上，还有各种各样的嘲弄。

sentences.en: So we have a question from, would you believe, Tom, we've got a question from Neville Chamberlain.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有一个问题，汤姆，你敢相信吗，我们有一个来自内维尔·张伯伦（Neville Chamberlain）的问题。

sentences.en: Neville Chamberlain says, were there any attempts by the Vikings to take over Byzantium in the same way they tried with England and Ireland?
sentences.zh: 内维尔·张伯伦曾问，维京人是否曾像试图征服英格兰和爱尔兰那样，试图征服拜占庭？

sentences.en: Neville, of course, his reaction would no doubt be to appease them.
sentences.zh: 内维尔的话，他的反应毫无疑问会是安抚他们。

sentences.en: A faraway country of which we know nothing.
sentences.zh: 一个我们一无所知的遥远国度。

sentences.en: And my answer to that would be, it's completely implausible they would ever take over Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 而我的回答是，他们想要征服君士坦丁堡是完全不可思议的。

sentences.en: There's one of them, isn't there, who nails his shield to the gates of Constantinople as a kind of gesture of contempt?
sentences.zh: 不是有那么一个人，把盾牌钉在君士坦丁堡的城门上，作为一种蔑视的姿态吗？

sentences.en: Because he obviously sees the walls as a kind of cheat.
sentences.zh: 因为他显然觉得这些城墙就像是一种作弊手段。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But he knows that they're never going to break in.
sentences.zh: 但他知道他们永远也攻不进去。

sentences.en: I mean, it's like saying, you know, will Paraguay ever defeat the United States and conquer its territory?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就像是说，巴拉圭有一天会击败美国并征服其领土一样？

sentences.en: I mean, it's just not a plausible matchup.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这根本不是一场势均力敌的较量。

sentences.en: I mean, so Mykligard, the great city, it's Constantinople comes to kind of shimmer in the imaginings of all the Vikings so much that essentially the Asgard, the city of the gods,
sentences.zh: 所以米克拉加德，那座伟大的城市，也就是君士坦丁堡，在所有维京人的想象中变得如此闪耀，以至于本质上，阿斯加德，那座众神之城，

sentences.en: comes to be equated with it.
sentences.zh: 开始与它画上等号。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that when they imagine what Odin's halls look like, they imagine it looking very like the golden city of Caesar.
sentences.zh: 所以当他们想象奥丁的大厅是什么样子时，他们想象它看起来非常像凯撒的黄金之城。

sentences.en: Don't they also, Tom, there are some people who think that when they talk about Asgard or they talk about Valhalla, that images of Hagia Sophia, the Church of the Holy Wisdom,
sentences.zh: 汤姆，难道没有一些人认为，当他们谈论阿斯加德或瓦尔哈拉时，圣索菲亚大教堂，也就是神圣智慧教堂的形象，

sentences.en: this incredible building, the biggest building in the Western world, I guess, at this point.
sentences.zh: 这座不可思议的建筑，我想在当时是西方世界最大的建筑。

sentences.en: Which we'll come to.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会讲到。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because it plays an important part in their story.
sentences.zh: 因为它在他们的故事中扮演了重要角色。

sentences.en: The gold, the mosaics, just the sort of, that creates a lot of the images of, because the images that we have of Valhalla or Asgard all come later, don't they?
sentences.zh: 黄金、马赛克，那种感觉，创造了许多意象，因为我们所拥有的关于瓦尔哈拉或阿斯加德的意象都是后来才出现的，不是吗？

sentences.en: They're all centuries after this.
sentences.zh: 它们都是几个世纪之后的事了。

sentences.en: And it seemed to kind of echo Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 而且它似乎与君士坦丁堡遥相呼应。

sentences.en: And I think the other difference, so there's no prospect of them capturing Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 我认为另一个区别在于，他们完全没有占领君士坦丁堡的希望。

sentences.en: But I think also what the Byzantine Empire can exert, which England or Ireland or even the Frankish Empire can't do, is to kind of generate this incredible cultural cringe.
sentences.zh: 但我认为拜占庭帝国所能施加的影响，是英格兰、爱尔兰甚至法兰克帝国都无法做到的，那就是产生一种令人难以置信的文化自卑感。

sentences.en: Because they, you know, every so often they're allowed, you know, they, it's actually with Constantine VII, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为他们，你知道，每隔一段时间他们就被允许，你知道，其实是在君士坦丁七世时期，对吧？

sentences.en: Who we mentioned in the previous episode, the emperor who describes this, the rapids that the Rus have to negotiate.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集提到过，那位描述罗斯人必须通过的急流的皇帝。

sentences.en: And he kind of concludes a treaty that specifies, you know, what they can trade, when they can trade, how they have to behave when they come.
sentences.zh: 他缔结了一项条约，规定了他们可以交易什么、何时交易、以及他们来的时候必须如何表现。

sentences.en: And they're kind of bringing in their walrus tusks and their narwhal tusks and their amber and their beeswax and all kinds of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们带来了海象牙、独角鲸牙、琥珀、蜂蜡以及各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: And they're also providing for what becomes very famous, a guard of what are called Varangians.
sentences.zh: 他们还提供了一种后来变得非常著名的卫队，被称为瓦兰吉亚卫队。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the Varangian, a var is a vow.
sentences.zh: 瓦兰吉亚人，var 是誓言的意思。

sentences.en: It's kind of like the English.
sentences.zh: 有点像英语。

sentences.en: The oath takers, would that be?
sentences.zh: 誓言承担者，是这样吗？

sentences.en: The oath takers.
sentences.zh: 誓言承担者。

sentences.en: And so they come to provide the emperor with his guard.
sentences.zh: 所以他们来为皇帝提供卫队。

sentences.en: And so the links, but essentially the Kievan Rus start to be absorbed into the kind of the cultural tractor beam of Byzantine culture.
sentences.zh: 所以这些联系，本质上基辅罗斯开始被吸入拜占庭文化的引力场中。

sentences.en: Well, that's where I would say, Tom, I'm sure you, I don't think this is a controversial view at all.
sentences.zh: 嗯，汤姆，我想说，我相信你也会同意，我不认为这是一个有争议的观点。

sentences.en: That's the point at which they stop being the Scandinavians who are known as the Rus and they start becoming the ancestors of Russia.
sentences.zh: 那就是他们不再是被称为罗斯人的斯堪的纳维亚人，而开始成为俄罗斯人的祖先的时刻。

sentences.en: Yeah, because they're brought into the world of orthodoxy, of Byzantine church architecture, of all those kinds.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为他们被带入了东正教的世界，带入了拜占庭的建筑风格，以及所有这些东西。

sentences.en: They're beginning to kind of contract marriage alliances and trade deals and all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们开始缔结联姻和贸易协定，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And that brings them, you know, what do they care about what's going on in Norway?
sentences.zh: 这让他们，你知道，他们还在乎挪威发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: I mean.
sentences.zh: 我是说。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so by the mid 10th century, you get the first ruler of Kiev.
sentences.zh: 所以到了10世纪中叶，你有了基辅的第一位统治者。

sentences.en: I'm going to have a go at this, Svietslav.
sentences.zh: 我要试着读一下，斯维亚托斯拉夫。

sentences.en: So he's the first ruler to have a Slavic name.
sentences.zh: 所以他是第一位拥有斯拉夫名字的统治者。

sentences.en: Slavic name.
sentences.zh: 斯拉夫名字。

sentences.en: But before him, you've had various rulers who have more obviously Norse names.
sentences.zh: 但在他之前，你已经有几位名字更明显的诺斯人的统治者了。

sentences.en: So we had Rurik.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有留里克。

sentences.en: That's golden deer with the guys who'd seized Kiev.
sentences.zh: 那是阿斯科尔德和迪尔，那些夺取基辅的人。

sentences.en: But then that gets seized from them by a guy called Oleg.
sentences.zh: 但后来它被一个叫奥列格的人从他们手中夺走了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Who is the guardian of Rurik's son, Igor, supposedly.
sentences.zh: 据说是留里克之子伊戈尔的监护人。

sentences.en: So Rurik is definitely Scandinavian.
sentences.zh: 所以留里克绝对是斯堪的纳维亚人。

sentences.en: And Oleg is also definitely Scandinavian because Oleg, which we always think of as a Russian name, is actually Helgi, I think.
sentences.zh: 而奥列格也绝对是斯堪的纳维亚人，因为我们总是认为奥列格是一个俄罗斯名字，但实际上它是海尔吉，我想。

sentences.en: Just like Olga is Helga.
sentences.zh: 就像奥尔加是海尔加一样。

sentences.en: So Helgi, or as we call him, Oleg, he's the guardian.
sentences.zh: 所以海尔吉，或者我们称他为奥列格，他是监护人。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's the guardian of Igor.
sentences.zh: 他是伊戈尔的监护人。

sentences.en: And Oleg is a very impressive man, generally.
sentences.zh: 而且奥列格通常是一个非常令人印象深刻的人。

sentences.en: He takes over Kiev.
sentences.zh: 他接管了基辅。

sentences.en: He seizes it from Asgold and Deer.
sentences.zh: 他从阿斯科尔德和迪尔手中夺取了它。

sentences.en: He leads another siege of Constantinople and gets a ton of money from sort of – so this is your parallel with the West, actually.
sentences.zh: 他领导了另一次对君士坦丁堡的围攻，并从那里得到了大量的钱财——所以这实际上是你与西方的平行之处。

sentences.en: He gets basically dangeled from the sort of Byzantine authorities in 904.
sentences.zh: 他在904年基本上从拜占庭当局那里得到了丹麦金。

sentences.en: But he has a most – they have very good deaths, the Grand Princes of Kiev.
sentences.zh: 但他有一个最——基辅大公们的死法都非常精彩。

sentences.en: So he has a very interesting death.
sentences.zh: 所以他有一个非常有趣的死法。

sentences.en: He has – he's been told, Oleg, that his favorite horse will be the cause of his death.
sentences.zh: 有人告诉奥列格，他最喜欢的马将是导致他死亡的原因。

sentences.en: So do you know what – do you know what Oleg does, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你知道奥列格做了什么吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Tell me.
sentences.zh: 告诉我。

sentences.en: He sends the horse away.
sentences.zh: 他把马送走了。

sentences.en: He says, you know, I don't want to kill it because it's my favorite horse.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，我不想杀它，因为它是我的爱马。

sentences.en: But send it away and look after it, and I'll never have any dealings with it again.
sentences.zh: 但把它送走照顾好，我再也不会和它有任何瓜葛了。

sentences.en: And after four years, in the year 914, he goes to see – he goes to visit the horse because he misses it so badly.
sentences.zh: 四年后，在914年，他去见——他去探望那匹马，因为他太想念它了。

sentences.en: It's so sad.
sentences.zh: 太令人难过了。

sentences.en: He goes to visit the horse at the stables, and he's told by the stable hands, well, the horse is dead.
sentences.zh: 他去马厩探望那匹马，马夫告诉他，马已经死了。

sentences.en: And he says, ha, ha, ha, you know.
sentences.zh: 他说，哈哈哈哈，你知道。

sentences.en: Cheated fate.
sentences.zh: 欺骗了命运。

sentences.en: Those astrologers were absolute muppets.
sentences.zh: 那些占星家真是彻头彻尾的笨蛋。

sentences.en: You know, I've cheated death.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我战胜了死亡。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he says, bring – to show my contempt for these soothsayers, bring me the skull of the horse.
sentences.zh: 他说，把——为了向这些预言家展示我的蔑视，把马的头骨拿来。

sentences.en: So they bring him the horse's skull.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把马的头骨拿给他。

sentences.en: And he stamps on it.
sentences.zh: 他踩在上面。

sentences.en: He's shouting, the horse is dead, but I am still alive.
sentences.zh: 他大喊着，马死了，但我还活着。

sentences.en: I was supposed to receive my death from this skull.
sentences.zh: 我本应从这个头骨中迎来我的死亡。

sentences.en: And he stamps on the horse, on the horse's skull.
sentences.zh: 他踩在马的头骨上。

sentences.en: And at that point, a snake crawls out from the horse's skull, bites him, and he dies.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，一条蛇从马的头骨里爬出来，咬了他，他就死了。

sentences.en: There you go.
sentences.zh: 你看，就是这样。

sentences.en: So the very act of defying the prophecy is what kills him.
sentences.zh: 所以正是这种蔑视预言的行为杀死了他。

sentences.en: But –
sentences.zh: 但是——

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he was guardian for Igor.
sentences.zh: 所以他是伊戈尔的监护人。

sentences.en: Yeah, so Igor then is – then takes over.
sentences.zh: 没错，所以伊戈尔随后接管了。

sentences.en: Igor has an even better death.
sentences.zh: 伊戈尔的死法更精彩。

sentences.en: Yeah, he has a very unfortunate death, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 没错，他的死法非常不幸，不是吗？

sentences.en: So Igor is the guy who negotiates the treaty with Constantine VII.
sentences.zh: 所以伊戈尔就是那个与君士坦丁七世谈判条约的人。

sentences.en: Because he's attacked them and been seen off with Greek fire, hasn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为他袭击了他们，结果被希腊火击退了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, he has.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Is that where he first used Greek fire?
sentences.zh: 那是他第一次使用希腊火吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which is what?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: Well, he twice – he does besiege Constantine Noble.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他两次——他确实围攻了君士坦丁堡。

sentences.en: He doesn't just attack, you know, with ships.
sentences.zh: 他不仅仅是用船只攻击，你知道。

sentences.en: He actually tries to take the city twice.
sentences.zh: 他实际上两次试图夺取这座城市。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he – basically, he's a very, very kind of expansionist guy.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是一个非常有扩张野心的人。

sentences.en: So he's also – it's in his reign that they all go off and plunder all the kind of Muslim cities on the Caspian Sea.
sentences.zh: 所以他也是——正是在他的统治期间，他们去洗劫了里海沿岸的所有穆斯林城市。

sentences.en: Oh, yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，没错。

sentences.en: They go to Azerbaijan, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们去了阿塞拜疆，对吧？

sentences.en: They go to Azerbaijan.
sentences.zh: 他们去了阿塞拜疆。

sentences.en: So he's all over the place.
sentences.zh: 所以他到处都是。

sentences.en: I mean, he's very keen on kicking sand in people's face.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他非常热衷于往别人脸上踢沙子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And one of the people that he kicks sand in the face of is a people called the Drevlians, or Slavic people.
sentences.zh: 而他往脸上踢沙子的人之一是一个叫德列夫利安人的民族，或者说是斯拉夫人。

sentences.en: And they capture him.
sentences.zh: 他们抓住了他。

sentences.en: They pull down two birch trees, and they tie him to the ends of these two trees.
sentences.zh: 他们拉下两棵桦树，把他绑在这两棵树的顶端。

sentences.en: And then they let the two birch trees go.
sentences.zh: 然后他们松开了这两棵桦树。

sentences.en: So he goes, and he gets split in two.
sentences.zh: 于是他被撕成了两半。

sentences.en: And that's the end of him.
sentences.zh: 这就是他的结局。

sentences.en: However, this is not a sensible thing to have done.
sentences.zh: 然而，这并不是一件明智的事情。

sentences.en: It's probably not true, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上这可能不是真的。

sentences.en: It's not true, that story.
sentences.zh: 那个故事不是真的。

sentences.en: Dominic.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克。

sentences.en: Now, center stage comes possibly the most interesting of all the rulers of Kiev, who is the wife of Igor and the mother of Svietslav, as he'll become.
sentences.zh: 现在，舞台中心出现了基辅所有统治者中可能最有趣的一位，她是伊戈尔的妻子，也是斯维亚托斯拉夫的母亲，正如他后来成为的那样。

sentences.en: He will become this ruler.
sentences.zh: 他将成为这位统治者。

sentences.en: But she is ruling as regent, Olga, Helga.
sentences.zh: 但她是以摄政王的身份统治的，奥尔加，海尔加。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You've got a bit of a torn dress for Olga, I think.
